target_customer: Home and commercial appliance repair servicers, including large authorized service companies
problem: Appliance servicers lose revenue on missed calls, slow scheduling and technician visits made without the right parts diagnosed in advance.
business_model: B2B software (AI employees) for service companies, integrated with existing field service management systems; pricing not public
product_category: AI phone, scheduling, dispatch and parts pre-identification for appliance repair

founders.name: Dan Katzman
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led strategy and operations at Nava Benefits.

founders.name: David Goodfellow
education: USC, BS in CS and BA
founders.background_notes: Engineering manager at Radar Labs leading fraud and geo-compliance products per YC page.

competitors.name: Fieldproxy
competitors.what: Field service software with AI scheduling and dispatch agents marketed to appliance repair shops

competitors.name: Vida
competitors.what: AI voice agent platform publishing an appliance repair guide on missed calls

competitors.name: Teneo.ai
competitors.what: Agentic AI launched for major household appliance brands

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents are widely available; the harder parts are integrating with field service systems, applying warranty and pricing rules, and the parts diagnosis model.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration with FSM and warranty feeds plus repair history data create stickiness, but generic AI phone agents are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many vendors market AI scheduling for appliance repair; no acquisition found for Bernard.

market_need_then: Appliance servicers face technician shortages, missed calls and low first-time fix rates; the company says it is live with some of the largest authorized service companies (company claim, no numbers).

branding.domain_note: Uses bernardhq.com, a suffix domain, rather than bernard.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical and operational; the site describes AI employees rather than hype

brand_strength.rationale: A human first name that is easy to say but generic and hard to search; no press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Bernard is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It targets a narrow vertical with a founding team combining operations and fraud engineering experience and a team of nine, but generic AI dispatch and voice products compete for the same buyers.
notes: Dealroom lists $125K and Simplify about $130K from one round; Simplify cites FundraisingFox naming Vela Partners, Y Combinator and Accel. All aggregator data, unverified, so no round recorded.
